articles.title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
articles.authors: Katsuhiro Ueno, Takumi Yomogida, Yuta Kumagai, Toru Kitagaki, Hirotomo Ikeuchi, Masato Mizokami, Shinya Mizokami
articles.summary: Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. …

articles.summary: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment. …

articles.title: Fatal pulmonary embolism following perineal hyaluronic acid injection for vaginoplasty: a case report
articles.authors: Jiang Y, Yun H, Du R, Qiu H, Liang M
institutions: Institute of Forensic Science of Tianjin Public Security
articles.summary: A 34-year-old woman collapsed one hour after an unlicensed vaginal tightening procedure involving hyaluronic acid (HA) injection performed in a non-medical setting. Clinical manifestations emerged with sudden syncope and transient loss of consciousness, followed by rapid hemodynamic deterioration upon hospital admission. The patient succumbed approximately three hours after admission. Postmortem histological examination identified extensive basophilic foreign material occluding local vaginal veins and pulmonary arteries. Histochemical analyses (Alcian blue pH 2.5, with and without hyaluronidase digestion) identified the material as HA. …

articles.summary: The liquid-phase synthesis of sulfide solid electrolytes has been hindered by an incomplete understanding of thiophosphate reaction pathways and the transient nature of reactive intermediates. Here, we report a stable liquid thiophosphate intermediate formed from Li2S and P4S10 in acetonitrile, enabling the rapid reaction to form Li6PS5Cl (LPSC) from a complete liquid phase. Combining in situ Raman spectroscopy, multinuclear NMR, and quantum chemical calculations, we identify a spectroscopically stable soluble thiophosphate intermediate and evaluate candidate structures consistent with its long-time solution behavior. …

articles.summary: This study aims to develop a method for the heterovalent doping of hydroxyapatite (HA) with europium (III) ions using laser fragmentation of a micropowder in a liquid medium. The samples examined after laser fragmentation of the hydroxyapatite micropowder in liquid exhibited ultrathin nanosheets (with an approximate thickness of 2–5 nm) while retaining the hydroxyapatite crystal structure; furthermore, when the process is carried out in a europium nitrate solution, it leads to the preferential incorporation of europium (III) ions into Ca(I) sites. The phase homogeneity and structural evolution of the fragmentation-derived samples were investigated by Raman and FTIR spectroscopy. …

articles.summary: The discovery of high-Tc superconductivity in Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate materials represented by La3Ni2O7 has opened new directions in the quest for unconventional superconductivity. A central unresolved issue concerns the pairing symmetry of the superconducting order. In this paper, we establish an experimentally accessible framework for discriminating between the two leading candidate gap symmetries in La3Ni2O7: a sign-changing s± state and a d-wave state. …

articles.summary: Lignin electro-oxidation at the anode offers a promising route to couple biomass valorization with low-voltage H 2 production, yet most reported systems rely on transition-metal catalysts. Here we show that simple acid engineering transforms commercial Vulcan carbon into an efficient metal-free anode for lignin electro-oxidation in alkaline media below 100 °C. Nitric acid treatment reveals an optimum surface state, with the 48 h-treated sample ( C-N(48) ) outperforming pristine carbon and other treatment times. …

To address this gap, our study aims to delve deeper into nanocrystal-enhancing mechanism, broadening understanding in this critical area. …

articles.authors: Shijie Ke, Zhangqi Dang, Xinrui Li, Jian Ge, Ziyang Zhang
articles.summary: Spectroscopy in the UVA band (315 nm-400 nm) is crucial for environmental monitoring and astronomical studies. Conventional UVA spectrometers are built using lenses and diffraction gratings. These bulky free-space optics may raise cost and maintenance issues for satellite observation systems. A compact spectrometer containing only fiber, chip, and camera is an attractive solution for robust and lightweight operation. Though waveguide-based spectrometers exist for the visible and infrared regions, migration toward the UV remains challenging due to material absorption and fabrication difficulties. …

articles.summary: Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectrometers enable rapid tea analysis, but the heterogeneity of tea leaves can reduce spectral representativeness and modelling reliability. This study evaluated the influence of sampling configurations on tea product discrimination and moisture prediction using two portable NIR spectrometers and developed a domain-specific NIR-analysis skill to support the analytical workflow. Ten tea products were analysed in ground and unground states using the NIR-R210 and NeoSpectra Scanner. Sixteen preprocessing methods were evaluated with partial least squares and support vector machine models. …

articles.summary: Molybdenum disulphide (MoS 2 ) is a semiconducting material whose vibrational and excitonic properties are highly sensitive to layer number and structural disorder. In this work, we demonstrate the possibility of producing MoS 2 monolayers on inert, electronics-compatible SiO 2 substrates via a room-temperature pulsed laser deposition (PLD) approach followed by post-annealing treatment. The fine controllability of the process parameters allows tuning the number of deposited layers from mono- to multilayer, and these systems have been systematically investigated using multiwavelength Raman spectroscopy. …
